name: WD 2226-210
description: WD 2226-210 is the central star of the Helix Nebula, about 216 parsecs away.

radius.source: González-Santamaría et al. (2021), A&A 656, A51, Table 8: log(L/Lsun) = 1.79 from the star's V magnitude at its Gaia EDR3 distance, and log(Teff) = 5.03; the paper prints no radius, and 0.0228 solar radii is the sphere that radiates that luminosity at that temperature (Stefan-Boltzmann law)

temperature.source: González-Santamaría et al. (2021), A&A 656, A51, Table 8: log(Teff) = 5.03, a temperature from the literature the paper compiles; spectral type DAO.5

gravity.source: Napiwotzki (1999), arXiv:astro-ph/9908181, Table 2: log g from a fit of the star's spectrum

distance.source: Benedict et al. (2009), HST parallaxes of planetary nebula nuclei: 216 pc (-12/+14) from the trigonometric parallax of this star, the distance its nebula's page stands at

text.card: WD 2226-210 is the central star of the Helix Nebula, about 216 parsecs away.
text.introduction: The Helix's central star shines at 107,000 K with 62 times the Sun's light. Its sphere is about two and a half times Earth's size.

notes: The star's mass is not measured. Evolutionary tracks give 0.57 solar masses from its spectrum (Napiwotzki (1999), arXiv:astro-ph/9908181, Table 2, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9908181).
A fit of its spectrum gives 103,600 K (Napiwotzki (1999), arXiv:astro-ph/9908181, Table 2, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9908181).
The luminosity behind the radius was computed at the star's Gaia EDR3 distance, about 200 pc. The page stands at 216 pc, where the same light needs a radius 8% larger.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6628874205642084224 (quality E), from 1953GCRV..C......0W; Gaia DR3 measures none
